thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: detected p99 decode latency spike >7s for streaming endpoints in us-west1. Triggered at 2026-03-15T10:02:00Z. Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat. SLO p99=2s.

marta: I'm on it — thanks bot. Are there any recent kernel or runtime deploys in the last 30m? Paging patterns?

deploy-bot: Deploy report: eng-runtime@v5.12.0 rolled 2026-03-15T09:45Z by mariam. Components: kernels/trt8-flashattn-optimized, compiler-flags=--optimize-memory,+--use-flash-attn.

ali: seeing p95 elevated (1.1s -> 1.9s) and p99 tail hits 6-8s. Traces point to decode stalls where KV cache tries to materialize pages. Feels like paging backpressure on GPU -> disk path.

jess: customer-ops: multiple enterprise customers reported 504s and streaming cutouts. CS has opened a high-priority ticket.

customer-ops: PayFlow reported ~120 failed stream requests in the window, they hit timeouts and retried. They've been notified that we're investigating.

mariam: confirmed the kernel + flag rollout earlier this morning. We exercised microbenchmarks but saw small variance; didn't catch this tail pattern at scale. No quantization changes.

samir: can we pin a rollback to the previous kernel build (trt8-stable) as a hotfix? Quick rollback seems fastest if it's kernel-regression.

ali: preparing rollback plan. Proposal: route 10% traffic to trt8-stable as canary, monitor p99 for 5m, then 100% if it improves. Also investigate allocator paging thresholds introduced in this kernel.

marta: do the canary. Also enable KV prefix warmup and raise local cache retention for streaming endpoints as a temporary mitigation.

code block: ```
2026-03-15T09:58:23Z [stream-worker-42] decode: tail latency 7420ms model=gpt-heavy kernel=trt8-flashattn flags=--optimize-memory
2026-03-15T09:58:24Z [stream-worker-19] pagefault: kvcache evict -> disk hit (read 12.6ms, retry stall)
2026-03-15T09:58:31Z [stream-worker-42] decode: resumed after pageback, kv pages loaded 1.2s
```

ali: running rollback commands now.

code block: ```
# rollback (hotfix)
deploy rollback eng-runtime 5.12.0 --to=eng-runtime@5.11.3 --component=kernels
# routing fallback for streaming
routing patch /v1/stream --model-fallback=trt8-stable --weights=0.9,0.1
```

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by ali at 1789500120. Canary routing set to 10% -> trt8-stable. Watching metrics.

jess: SRE note: GPU mem churn graphs show higher allocation churn after the kernel change and more frequent pagefaults. Disk IO increased on the kv-store nodes during the spike window.

mariam: I can repro a degraded tail locally with bursty sequence lengths. nvprof shows higher kernel preemption in the flashattn path when sequence-length distribution spikes — leads to context switch thrash and temporary KV misses. Investigating a fix.

ali: initial canary numbers: p99 trending down from 7.4s -> 2.8s on the 10% canary within 3m. If that continues, we'll complete rollback.

marta: good. Keep me posted. CS: send a short status update to PayFlow and flag incident in the dashboard.

customer-ops: Sent status to PayFlow, ticket #12345 updated: "Investigating streaming latency, tentative mitigation in progress (kernel rollback)."

oncall-next: I'm on shift in ~30m, will take the handoff if still open. Please leave action items and current hypothesis.

samir: action items: (1) finish rollback to trt8-stable if canary holds, (2) reproduce failure with synthetic streaming bursts, (3) instrument kernel pagefault path and add counters, (4) build patch to reduce allocator eviction aggression in trt8-flashattn.

marta: adding monitoring playbook: increase retention for tail traces for the stream cluster for next 24h and alert on pgfault rate > 0.5/min.

incident-bot: UPDATE: p99 improved to ~2.8s after partial rollback. Monitoring continues. Incident status: mitigation in progress.

ali: will post postmortem pointer when we have the root cause. If rollback completes OK, we'll keep trt8-stable for prod while mariam prepares a patched kernel build.

mariam: noted, I'll start a kernel patch branch and run large-scale streaming load tests. Expect initial PR within 6-8 hours.

marta: thanks team — handing off to oncall-next in 30m. Keep the channel updated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: ongoing (mitigation in progress). Triage lead: marta. Severity: S3 (customer-impacting latency).
